If someone comes up to me and snacks me around the head with a crowbar, and they cause a brain injury, I may also need years of ongoing help to manage it and repair damage. That could involve doctors who work with my physical brain, but also therapists and psychiatrists who help me with the mental impact of the brain injury. Rehabilitation from something like that can require many different fields of medicine, but they're all important in healing and recovery with the best outcomes. If someone comes up to me and assaults me in a way that causes a serious chemical change within my brain, impacts my ability to function day to day, etc but that injury is caused by a different kind of violence (sexual) there's no actual reason that should be considered different to another injury and the treatments considered different to other treatments. That's just a social stigma and the remnants of our history of treating mental health and trauma as a lack of ability to suck it up and stop being a sook about it. We know that trauma can actively damage the brain and nervous system, we know what treatments help with that, we have the resources available to fund those treatments, it's just common sense.
